## 7. Human expertise, recruitment, disagreement and labor

[analysis] Expertise has at least four operational components: eligibility, task familiarity, calibrated judgment and permission to perform the work. The inspected sources use different proxies: Turing describes identity/background/work-history verification; Shaip describes credentials and a calibration gate; Encord describes task-to-domain matching; Prolific offers verified experience or targeted assessments. These are not one standardized credential. For each task, ask which evidence predicts successful completion and which screening merely establishes identity or administrative eligibility.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.supplier.turing.verification](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.turing.verification), [candidate.cohort3.shaip.expert-matching](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort3.shaip.expert-matching), [candidate.cohort3.shaip.calibration-gate](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort3.shaip.calibration-gate), [candidate.cohort3.encord.expert-matching](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort3.encord.expert-matching), [candidate.supplier.prolific.ai-taskers](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.prolific.ai-taskers)

[analysis] Recruitment and contribution remain separate stages. HelpSteer3 names different recruitment/annotation roles for Scale and Translated; Prolific’s studied role is recruitment into a researcher-owned interface; U-MATH credits Toloka AI and Gradarius with validation of professor-authored problems. A contributor manifest should record authoring, recruitment, labeling, review, adjudication and final release authority separately. Affiliation, acknowledgments or a capability page alone should not be used to infer a contribution edge.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.scale-subset-recruitment](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.scale-subset-recruitment), [candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.translated-subset-recruitment](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.translated-subset-recruitment), [candidate.supplier.prolific.cohere-recruitment](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.prolific.cohere-recruitment), [candidate.supplier.toloka.umath-validation](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.toloka.umath-validation)

[analysis] The human experiment on instruction-tuning disagreement uses the same annotators and items for individual ratings and paired preferences, yet reports different ambiguity patterns and no evidence in that setup that preference annotation is easier. This cautions against assuming that a change from scales to pairs resolves judgment ambiguity. A pilot should test the intended formulation with representative difficult items, retain task-specific reasons and distinguish unclear instructions from legitimate preference diversity.

Evidence IDs: [cohort3.claim.disagreement.matched-design](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.disagreement.matched-design), [cohort3.claim.disagreement.instance-disagreement](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.disagreement.instance-disagreement), [cohort3.claim.disagreement.agreement-not-superiority](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.disagreement.agreement-not-superiority)

[analysis] DICES separates two rater pools and applies explicit quality exclusions, while its expert reference can disagree with crowd majority. The Minority Reports paper defines a minority relative to final majority consensus and warns that RLHF preference tasks may lack a single clear ground truth. Together these sources support keeping minority labels inspectable. They do not establish that every disagreement is valuable or that a majority is always wrong. The analyst recommendation is to adjudicate the reason for disagreement before filtering the person who expressed it.

Evidence IDs: [cohort3.claim.dices.two-pools](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.dices.two-pools), [cohort3.claim.dices.quality-filter](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.dices.quality-filter), [cohort3.claim.dices.expert-crowd-difference](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.dices.expert-crowd-difference), [cohort8.claim.minority.minority-definition](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.minority.minority-definition), [cohort8.claim.minority.rlhf-boundary](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.minority.rlhf-boundary)

[sourced_fact] The approved Minority Reports pruning observation is scoped to the §5.1 prose: unseen workers or tasks are retained, while otherwise the estimated minority-report probability is compared with a threshold. The reviewed Algorithm 1 line and surrounding prose have a documented consistency concern in the source review. This report does not certify that pseudocode and prose are equivalent. The simulation reference compares post-pruning majority votes with the counterfactual unpruned majority, rather than establishing an external truth label for every judgment.

Evidence IDs: [cohort8.claim.minority.cold-start-retain](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.minority.cold-start-retain), [cohort8.claim.minority.evaluation-reference](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.minority.evaluation-reference)

[analysis] Calibration and adjudication should have separate logs. Appen describes gold questions and adjudication; DataForce describes automated checks, consensus and expert adjudication; Snorkel describes calibration and dual-expert review; Shaip describes sampled blind double-labeling and weekly agreement reports. Request the raw judgments before consensus, the rule for escalation, the adjudicator’s independence and the number of corrected accepted units. A final agreement percentage is a process output whose meaning depends on those rules, not a universal reliability score.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.supplier.appen.adjudication](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.appen.adjudication), [candidate.cohort2.dataforce.selection-adjudication](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort2.dataforce.selection-adjudication), [repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.quality-controls](evidence.html#assertion-repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.quality-controls), [candidate.cohort3.shaip.sampled-qa](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort3.shaip.sampled-qa)

[analysis] Training instructions are themselves a research input. The reviewed factorial study crosses instruction design with incentives and measures accuracy, helpfulness and difficulty separately. Data Cascades examines high-stakes data-work failures; CrowdWorkSheets asks why an annotator pool fits intended uses and impacted communities. These works motivate testing guideline clarity and the consequences of exclusion before scaling. They do not establish a universal wage or training-duration effect for all suppliers. Intervention results should retain task, sample, payment and outcome definitions.

Evidence IDs: [cohort7.claim.instructions.factorial](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.instructions.factorial), [cohort7.claim.instructions.measures](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.instructions.measures), [cohort7.claim.instructions.payments](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.instructions.payments), [cohort8.claim.crowdworksheets.selection-rationale](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.crowdworksheets.selection-rationale), [cohort3.claim.cascades.four-categories](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.cascades.four-categories), [cohort3.claim.cascades.design-limits](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.cascades.design-limits)

[analysis] Multilingual coverage must be tested at the intersection of language, domain, rubric and modality. HelpSteer3 identifies missing domain intersections; M-IFEval removes language-inappropriate constraints and uses native-speaker leads; BenchMAX uses human post-editing of translations; MENLO separates fluency, tone and localized factuality. Translation of a single English benchmark is not evidence that every language variant measures the same construct. A buyer should sample required intersections and use native-domain review before claiming coverage.

Evidence IDs: [repair20261111.claim.current-reference145](evidence.html#assertion-repair20261111.claim.current-reference145), [cohort7.claim.mifeval.japanese-filter](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.mifeval.japanese-filter), [cohort7.claim.mifeval.language-leads](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.mifeval.language-leads), [cohort7.claim.benchmax.pipeline](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.benchmax.pipeline), [cohort7.claim.menlo.dimensions](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.menlo.dimensions)

[analysis] Model-judge agreement is also conditional. The multilingual-judge study uses parallel ground-truth answers, pointwise criteria and a particular prompting setup, with cross-language consistency measured by treating language-specific judgments as raters. M-RewardBench translates general-task instances with human-reviewed filtering and separately uses human-rated translation pairs. These are different validation designs. Neither supports an unqualified conclusion that an English-calibrated judge is reliable in every locale or that translated evaluation is equivalent to native task authoring.

Evidence IDs: [cohort7.claim.multijudge.parallel-answers](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.multijudge.parallel-answers), [cohort7.claim.multijudge.pointwise](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.multijudge.pointwise), [cohort7.claim.multijudge.prompt](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.multijudge.prompt), [cohort7.claim.multijudge.agreement](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.multijudge.agreement), [cohort7.claim.mreward.translation](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.mreward.translation), [cohort7.claim.mreward.maple](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.mreward.maple)

[analysis] Pool statistics should not become labor statistics. Appen’s global crowd, Mercor’s advertised expert network, Turing’s advertised pool, TELUS Digital’s community membership and Prolific’s active/waitlist figures have different definitions. None should be converted into the number of people who earned money this week, the number available for a specific assignment or the number of accepted tasks. A useful labor ledger distinguishes registered profiles, screened people, matched people, active paid contributors, attempted units, accepted units and paid units under explicit windows.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.supplier.appen.crowd-network](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.appen.crowd-network), [repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.candidate.supplier.mercor.expert-pool](evidence.html#assertion-repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.candidate.supplier.mercor.expert-pool), [candidate.supplier.turing.expert-pool](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.turing.expert-pool), [candidate.cohort2.telus_digital.community-pool](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort2.telus_digital.community-pool), [repair20261111.claim.current-reference221](evidence.html#assertion-repair20261111.claim.current-reference221)

[analysis] Workforce arrangement changes the questions to ask. Sama describes full-time in-house delivery; TELUS Digital lists several workforce modes; Alegion describes workforce partners; Scale describes BPOs and proprietary platforms; isahit describes self-employed onboarding. These descriptions cannot establish legal status or worker experience across jurisdictions. For a project, record the contracting entity, subcontracting chain, training obligation, supervision, payment authority and appeal channel rather than assume the same conditions from a shared annotation label.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.cohort2.sama.employee-delivery](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort2.sama.employee-delivery), [repair20261111.claim.current-reference176](evidence.html#assertion-repair20261111.claim.current-reference176), [candidate.cohort3.alegion.partner-workforce](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort3.alegion.partner-workforce), [repair20261111.claim.current-reference119](evidence.html#assertion-repair20261111.claim.current-reference119), [candidate.cohort3.isahit.onboarding-status](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort3.isahit.onboarding-status)

[analysis] Compensation disclosures concern different units and conditions. Prolific publishes permitted minimum and recommended participant hourly rates; Handshake puts amount, type and timing in project invitations; Humans in the Loop uses supervisor-approved delivered units; Snorkel describes weekly HireArt processing of prior accepted work, aims for processing within two weeks after acceptance, and allows project-dependent variation; micro1 states a twice-monthly schedule. These are rules or schedules, not comparable realized wages. Any labor analysis should count qualification, waiting, revisions, rejections and administrative time separately and retain the project’s currency and payment basis.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.supplier.prolific.minimum-rewards](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.prolific.minimum-rewards), [candidate.cohort4.handshake_ai.project-payment-basis](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort4.handshake_ai.project-payment-basis), [candidate.cohort3.humans_in_the_loop.unit-payment-basis](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort3.humans_in_the_loop.unit-payment-basis), [repair.qualbinding.20261111.v2.candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.payment-and-choice](evidence.html#assertion-repair.qualbinding.20261111.v2.candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.payment-and-choice), [candidate.cohort4.micro1.expert-payment-schedule](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort4.micro1.expert-payment-schedule)

[analysis] Sensitive-content and monitoring rules deserve operational evidence. Scale describes notice, the ability to decline and wellness resources; Toloka requires disclosure and acknowledgement before labeling; the dated Welo case describes informed consent; Invisible discloses keystroke, screenshot and webcam collection with possible access consequences if declined. These sources describe different settings. They do not prove that every worker could safely refuse, obtained support or experienced proportionate monitoring. A buyer should request project notices, escalation handling and aggregate worker-feedback evidence without seeking unnecessary personal records.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.supplier.scale_ai.sensitive-content](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.scale_ai.sensitive-content), [candidate.supplier.toloka.sensitive-content](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.toloka.sensitive-content), [candidate.cohort2.welocalize.sensitive-content-consent](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort2.welocalize.sensitive-content-consent), [candidate.cohort2.invisible.work-monitoring](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort2.invisible.work-monitoring)

[analysis] Labor research has its own sampling limits. The Data-Production Dispositif combines interviews, observation and instruction-document analysis in specific Latin American settings; the Latin American labor article states that unknown platform-population boundaries limit statistical representativeness; the requester-proxy study limits its conclusions to US requester perspectives and self-reports. These studies illuminate mechanisms and research questions. They should not become global percentages, a census of all workers or evidence that a named supplier currently practices every behavior described.

Evidence IDs: [cohort7.claim.dataproduction.fieldwork](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.dataproduction.fieldwork), [cohort7.claim.dataproduction.sites](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.dataproduction.sites), [cohort8.claim.latinlabour.representativeness](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.latinlabour.representativeness), [cohort8.claim.proxies.self-report-limit](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.proxies.self-report-limit)

[research_gap] Important labor unknowns remain: independently measured effective pay, qualification rejection and appeal outcomes, subcontractor payment reconciliation, harmful-content exposure, contributor retention and the relation between monitoring and acceptance. The public-source corpus does not resolve these for the covered market. Research can progress through consented worker studies, project-level anonymized logs and comparable definitions, while avoiding inference from registered pools or recruitment advertisements.

[analysis] Disagreement routing should distinguish uncertainty from error. Experts Rise uses cross-model entropy to select expert attention, while Inherent Disagreements models multiple interpretations of the same short sentence pairs. CrowdTruth defines mutually dependent consistency scores but leaves broader comparative validation open. The practical choice is whether the task seeks one verifiable answer, a distribution of valid interpretations or a codebook revision. Record that choice before using disagreement to exclude workers, remove items or declare a quality improvement.

[analysis] Instruction design and assistance need separate acceptance checks. The surgical study’s comparison is conditional on instruction richness and project-specific QA; LabelAId’s intervention improves precision within a 34-person study without an equivalence finding on time. Neither supports a general staffing reduction. In a proposed pilot, log instruction revisions, assistance shown, human corrections and downstream acceptance, then inspect whether the intervention changes errors or merely which cases remain. Preserve any effect on contributor effort and disagreement as part of the operating record.

[analysis] Qualification labor is part of the production process. The qualification-threshold study observes task-dependent effects and self-selection; CrowdSpeech/VoxDIY reports compensation for attempted exams and completed pre-block tasks; the writers study makes revision and interaction visible. The analyst judgment is to budget and record qualification, calibration, waiting, revision and rejected-but-payable work separately from accepted-unit production. Confidence is moderate in the relevance of that accounting and unestablished for any supplier’s actual effective pay. Consented paid-time logs and task-specific performance comparisons would change the labor assessment.

[analysis] Human expert and model persona are different provenance categories. U-MATH describes mathematical experts reviewing tasks; APEX-Agents records expert creation and independent baselines; RIFT’s taxonomy uses human expert annotations while its scoring panels are generated expert personas. A contract should state which decisions require a credentialed person, whether review is independent of authorship and how unresolved judgments are escalated. Confidence is high in those distinctions and unmeasured for outcome superiority. Blinded assessment of raw expert decisions, panel disagreement and final accepted artifacts would change the staffing design.

StereoTales compares multilingual generated associations with one UK English-language panel; AttuneBench has repeated conversations from eleven participants; the personality study measures model questionnaire responses rather than human personalities. The 2010 annotation-methodology paper warns about undocumented instructions and reconciliation drift; SciCode adds out-of-domain clarity review; GeneBench-Pro reports changes to data-generating processes or ground truth after expert review. [analysis] Human contribution should remain stage-specific when a collection also uses models. Multi-SWE-bench reports outsourced annotation and internal engineering review without naming an outsourcing supplier; ScienceVision reports Elorian AI/UniPat AI joint construction and an annotation pool without establishing compensation or independent credential checks; s1K credits a person for generating model traces without establishing paid label work. The inference is to record actual task authoring, labeling, review, recruitment, trace generation and funding roles independently. Confidence is high in avoiding transitive supplier attribution and unknown for undisclosed contracts. Project-specific agreements and role records could resolve particular commercial relationships.

[analysis] Expert-review intensity is useful process evidence but does not supply a shared quality measure. GDPval describes iterative human reviews; HSS admits candidates after unanimous independent review rounds; Riemann-Bench asks two experts to solve each problem without the author’s solution. Their different task populations, acceptance rules and reviewer information prevent a ranking by the number of reviewers alone. A buyer should retain which reviewers saw earlier answers, how disagreement changed the task and which candidates were removed. Confidence is high that these fields are needed to interpret the process; comparative error reduction is unmeasured. Independent post-release error sampling could test whether the retained process predicts delivered correctness.

## 8. Commercial evidence and procurement economics

[sourced_fact] Appen — reported revenue. The audited FY2025 statements report consolidated customer-contract revenue of USD 230.774 million for 1 January–31 December 2025, including Appen Global USD 127.874 million and Appen China USD 102.900 million. These geographic operating segments do not isolate expert generative-AI data or the market definition used in this report. The figures are full-year reported revenue, not annualized pace, gross transaction volume, contributor pay or a comparable human-feedback segment across suppliers.

[sourced_fact] Proximal — annualized pace. Its 29 September 2026 announcement reports $200 million in annualized revenue. The inspected disclosure does not specify an ISO currency code, annualization window, gross-versus-net basis or revenue split by business line. It is self-reported pace, not an audited annual revenue total, profit, bookings, valuation or contractor payout. No annual recognized-revenue amount is calculated from it in this report.

Its FY2025 statement, approved in June 2026, reports nearly $1 billion paid to hundreds of thousands of contributors across more than 150 countries to date. The statement does not define a start/end period or a dollar currency code for that aggregate, and payment reconciliation was not inspected. The number is not annual revenue, annual labor cost, a current paid-active workforce total or a wage estimate.

The 14 October 2026 company announcement reports more than $100 million in Series E financing comprising equity and a credit facility, at a $1.25 billion pre-money valuation. The inspected source uses dollar symbols without an explicit ISO currency. The facility is not equity, and financing and valuation are not revenue or evidence of accepted data volume. No implied annual growth or provider-performance score is calculated.

[sourced_fact] Prolific — tariff and reward rules. The captured FAQ states usual platform fees of 42.8% for corporate customers and 33.3% for academic/nonprofit customers, but the bound passage does not explicitly state the percentage denominator. It separately sets minimum participant rewards of GBP 6 or USD 8 per hour and recommends GBP 9 or USD 12, with higher expert compensation recommended. Managed services are custom-priced. These are published rules and tariff disclosures rather than realized earnings, margins or a complete specialist-project quote.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.supplier.prolific.fees](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.prolific.fees), [candidate.supplier.prolific.minimum-rewards](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.prolific.minimum-rewards)

[sourced_fact] Other disclosed billing units differ. Prime Intellect’s Model Factory terms meter allocated GPU-hours prorated to the second, with rates in the order or platform; personnel post-training needs a separate professional-services order. A.Team lists hourly and other builder-engagement models. Terac describes expert payout plus a platform fee and separately monthly USD payment per verified completion for partnerships. AfterQuery reserves fees to order forms or separate agreements. These documents describe commercial structure, not a comparable price per accepted preference pair or environment.

Evidence IDs: [repair.binding.v1.candidate.cohort4.prime_intellect.gpu-billing-basis](evidence.html#assertion-repair.binding.v1.candidate.cohort4.prime_intellect.gpu-billing-basis), [candidate.cohort4.prime_intellect.professional-service-separation](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort4.prime_intellect.professional-service-separation), [candidate.cohort5.a-team.delivery-model](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort5.a-team.delivery-model), [candidate.cohort5.terac.buyer-billing-model](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort5.terac.buyer-billing-model), [candidate.cohort5.terac.partner-payment-basis](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort5.terac.partner-payment-basis), [candidate.cohort4.afterquery.separate-service-pricing](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort4.afterquery.separate-service-pricing)

[analysis] The analytical rule is to keep commercial denominators separate. A company-wide annualized rate cannot be divided by a benchmark count to estimate task price; cumulative payouts cannot identify a current take rate; financing cannot measure demand; a broad expert pool cannot be a capacity denominator. The selected disclosures support questions for diligence, not supplier market shares. A defensible future comparison would need the same reporting period, currency, gross/net basis, organizational segment and accepted-unit definition across every included provider.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.supplier.appen.revenue-fy2025](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.appen.revenue-fy2025), [repair.binding.v1.candidate.cohort4.proximal.annualized-revenue-disclosure](evidence.html#assertion-repair.binding.v1.candidate.cohort4.proximal.annualized-revenue-disclosure), [candidate.supplier.scale_ai.cumulative-payout](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.scale_ai.cumulative-payout), [candidate.cohort2.labelbox.financing](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort2.labelbox.financing), [repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.candidate.supplier.mercor.expert-pool](evidence.html#assertion-repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.candidate.supplier.mercor.expert-pool)

[method] Reproducible buyer calculation: accepted-unit cost equals all attributable project cash costs divided by independently accepted units. The numerator should state whether it includes recruitment, qualification, paid training, tool licenses, compute, project management, review, rework and buyer-side acceptance. The denominator should identify the unit: independent judgment, resolved item, trajectory, verified environment, recorded hour or licensed release. This is a proposed accounting method; the report does not insert hypothetical numbers or claim observed costs for suppliers.

[method] Reproducible review calculation: first-pass acceptance equals accepted units on first submission divided by all submitted units; final acceptance equals accepted units after permitted rework divided by all submitted units. Keep attempt, exclusion and unresolved counts. For expert-time projects, report both accepted outputs per paid hour and buyer QA effort per accepted output, without interpreting either as worker wages. For environment projects, separate authoring, maintenance, execution and recurring license costs, and preserve the term of access.

[method] Procurement comparison procedure: issue the same task brief and acceptance rubric, obtain responsibility and rights schedules, run a paid calibration sample, then quote a frozen production scope. Compare totals only after normalizing included review/rework and access terms. Log scope changes as new versions rather than treating a renegotiated specification as supplier underperformance. Proposed service-level thresholds should come from the buyer’s loss tolerance and pilot uncertainty; they are not reported market standards.

[research_gap] The commercial research gap is task-matched economics. This corpus does not supply comparable current contracts, realized gross/net human-data revenue, project margins, cancellation/rework charges or accepted-unit costs across suppliers. Missing financial disclosure is unknown rather than zero. No financial forecast, market-size projection, provider-return model or inferred valuation multiple is warranted by this evidence.

[analysis] Cost comparisons must include the measured boundary. LMCrowd excludes model, prompt and worker selection from its tariff comparison; CrowdAgent holds human annotation proportions rather than all computation or operating cost equal. HelpSteer2 discards about half of collected annotations overall, so accepted responses and purchased ratings have different denominators. Request setup, failed/rejected work, QA, adjudication, model calls, compute and accepted-unit totals explicitly. These studies inform accounting questions; they do not provide current service prices or a cross-provider cost ranking.

Evidence IDs: [cohort9.claim.lmcrowd.cost-boundary](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.lmcrowd.cost-boundary), [cohort9.claim.crowdagent.fixed-human-ratios](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.crowdagent.fixed-human-ratios), [cohort9.claim.helpsteer2.agreement-selection](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.helpsteer2.agreement-selection)

[analysis] Worker-time accounting is also distinct from project billing. The historical MTurk log study produces different work-unit rates under accept-to-submit and temporal-cluster definitions; its task/cluster medians are not median worker wages. Selected plugin users, unknown active effort and noncausal associations constrain inference. For a new project, request consented, task-appropriate compensation and time evidence rather than convert historical platform figures or supplier revenue into a claim about present worker earnings.

Evidence IDs: [cohort9.claim.earnings.wage-definition](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.earnings.wage-definition), [cohort9.claim.earnings.work-unit-wages](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.earnings.work-unit-wages), [cohort9.claim.earnings.causality-limit](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.earnings.causality-limit)

[analysis] Cost comparison must preserve generation, verification and acceptance budgets. Weaver generates 100 candidates per query and can call many verifiers; APEX-SWE averages repeated one-hour task runs; APEX-Agents evaluates repeated attempts; DAYJOB excludes error attempts from its score and uses creator-estimated healthcare time and a separately reported finance mean. These choices affect measured performance and a buyer’s cost ledger differently. Confidence is high that a single score or token bill is insufficient and unestablished for relative supplier unit costs. Record all attempted work, retries, judge calls, human escalation and accepted outputs before estimating a project-specific cost per usable unit. DAYJOB’s reported agent/condenser call cost excludes the judge and is not an all-in service price.

[analysis] Reported professional-task performance is not revenue or observed economic output. DAYJOB’s healthcare times are creator estimates; its finance mean has a separate dataset-card basis; APEX-Accounting measures rubric completion and repeated reliability on selected synthetic worlds; PLE reports a mean hybrid score. Multiplying those scores by an occupation’s wages would introduce unmeasured task representativeness, deployment overhead, review, failure cost and acceptance assumptions. ## 9. Rights, security, privacy and attribution governance

[analysis] Dataset rights should be modeled as a chain of permissions rather than a single badge. The Data Provenance Initiative distinguishes creator-attributable data licenses from code licenses and explicitly limits itself to best-effort self-reported categorization. Common Pile requires confidence that license information originates with a rights holder. These methods support asking who can grant which rights for each component, transformation and release. They do not establish enforceability or replace project-specific legal review.

Evidence IDs: [cohort3.claim.provenance.data-license-protocol](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.provenance.data-license-protocol), [cohort3.claim.provenance.scope-caveat](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.provenance.scope-caveat), [cohort7.claim.commonpile.licensor](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.commonpile.licensor)

[analysis] Web availability and collection permission are distinct. Consent in Crisis reports inconsistencies between robots.txt signals and terms of service in selected corpora. Documenting C4 recommends documenting included and excluded text and leaves some PII/copyright auditing to future work. FineWeb and Dolma acknowledge residual harmful or sensitive content despite filtering. A buyer should retain capture-time permissions, exclusion rules and removal paths, while treating a crawlable page as a source observation rather than automatic authorization to train or redistribute.

[analysis] License scope can change within a research artifact. AlpacaEval declares different code and data licenses; RewardBench aggregation remains subject to component terms; MathVista retains original image/question copyright and prohibits training use; GAIA asks against public redistribution. The correct unit for diligence is the exact component and use, not a repository’s top-level license string. A restrictive finding does not imply that this report possesses or can redistribute the underlying data.

Evidence IDs: [cohort2.dataset.claim.alpacaeval.component-license](evidence.html#assertion-cohort2.dataset.claim.alpacaeval.component-license), [next.claim.rewardbench.terms](evidence.html#assertion-next.claim.rewardbench.terms), [cohort4.dataset.claim.mathvista.terms](evidence.html#assertion-cohort4.dataset.claim.mathvista.terms), [repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.cohort4.dataset.claim.gaia.gate](evidence.html#assertion-repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.cohort4.dataset.claim.gaia.gate)

[analysis] Customer material and website visitor data have different policy boundaries. AfterQuery explicitly excludes processor/service-provider customer processing from its website policy; Mercor excludes its work platform; Label Your Data and LXT describe client-instruction processing; Proximal requires written consent and an executed agreement for generalized-model use of customer material. Obtain the project processing agreement, subprocessors, retention and secondary-use terms. A public policy’s existence does not establish that the proposed delivery is covered by every described safeguard.

[sourced_fact] Entity names and terms require exact scope. Kili’s May 2025 legal notice names MYAI SAS, while its same-date EULA names KILI-TECHNOLOGY SAS under the same Paris registration number; the public inconsistency is unresolved. DDD’s published Terms of Use name DDD Ventures LLC and use investment/real-estate language, so that page does not settle the AI-data contracting identity. iSoftStone’s privacy policy identifies a website-scoped US operator without resolving ultimate ownership or group-wide contracting responsibility. These findings preserve uncertainty rather than invent corporate transactions or additional suppliers.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.cohort6.kili_technology.published-operator-name](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort6.kili_technology.published-operator-name), [candidate.cohort6.digital_divide_data.legal-page-discrepancy](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort6.digital_divide_data.legal-page-discrepancy), [candidate.cohort6.isoftstone.website-operator](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort6.isoftstone.website-operator)

[analysis] Secondary use and human access can be explicit commercial conditions. Datasaur’s terms contain a free-access deidentified/aggregate improvement exception; Deploy’s terms default to manual Hive Worker review of customer content unless otherwise agreed in writing; Dataocean’s website policy leaves product/project rules to the corresponding services. None of these clauses alone establishes what happened to a particular customer’s records. A buyer should identify the applicable subscription, written exceptions, worker exposure, use permissions and service-specific privacy terms before choosing a delivery path.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.cohort6.datasaur.customer-data-use-scope](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort6.datasaur.customer-data-use-scope), [candidate.cohort6.hive.manual-review-default](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort6.hive.manual-review-default), [candidate.cohort6.speechocean.website-privacy-scope](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort6.speechocean.website-privacy-scope)

[sourced_fact] Toloka’s published task guidelines distinguish public-space images, third-party personal information and personal information collected from Tolokers. For third-party information, the listed conditions include both anonymization before upload and consent agreements. Collection from Tolokers also carries lawful-collection, administering-entity, purpose and policy conditions. These are category-specific platform rules, not a finding that every dataset complies. The linked additional collection guidelines were not separately captured in the reviewed scope.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.supplier.toloka.pii-rules](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.toloka.pii-rules)

[analysis] Biometric and authorship metadata deserve separate consent and use records. Toloka’s notice bases identity matching on explicit consent and says refusal can prevent onboarding; it also discloses authorship metadata in some coding deliverables. Turing’s policy lists AI development/training uses of personal information, while Polymath excludes interview voice recordings and transcripts from model training. These statements concern different records and services. Preserve which person, purpose, data type and downstream use each notice covers rather than combine them into a general permission claim.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.supplier.toloka.biometric-consent](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.toloka.biometric-consent), [candidate.supplier.toloka.client-code-metadata](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.toloka.client-code-metadata), [candidate.supplier.turing.personal-data-ai-use](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.turing.personal-data-ai-use), [candidate.cohort4.polymath_ai_labs.interview-training-restriction](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort4.polymath_ai_labs.interview-training-restriction)

[analysis] Security disclosure must retain attestation type and scope. Scale states SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO/IEC 27001:2022; Appen describes SOC 2 Type II, a HIPAA-specific solution and facility options; Snorkel states SOC 2 Type 2 and engagement-start scoping; Prolific describes ISO 27001 and Cyber Essentials while treating SOC 2 Type 2 as a future plan. Underlying reports, certificate scopes and customer deployments were not inspected here. These statements should not be flattened into equivalent independently verified controls.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.supplier.scale_ai.security-disclosure](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.scale_ai.security-disclosure), [repair20261111.claim.current-reference078](evidence.html#assertion-repair20261111.claim.current-reference078), [repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.security-scope](evidence.html#assertion-repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.security-scope), [candidate.supplier.prolific.security](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.prolific.security)

[analysis] Operational controls can be tiered or project-specific. CloudFactory distinguishes included network controls from optional endpoint controls; Sama describes assigned-employee project rooms; Encord describes role permissions; DataForce’s vendor notice requires an applicable DPA before EU-personal-data processing. A buyer should verify the selected tier, location, legal entity, access matrix and actual data flow. The report records disclosed controls, without certifying that all personnel or projects implement them.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.cohort2.cloudfactory.network-baseline](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort2.cloudfactory.network-baseline), [candidate.cohort2.cloudfactory.endpoint-controls](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort2.cloudfactory.endpoint-controls), [repair20261111.claim.current-reference094](evidence.html#assertion-repair20261111.claim.current-reference094), [candidate.cohort3.encord.access-roles](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort3.encord.access-roles), [candidate.cohort2.dataforce.vendor-dpa](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort2.dataforce.vendor-dpa)

[analysis] Incidents and remediation should be compared on evidence, not on whether one company has a public disclosure. Mercor’s company investigation account describes the March 2026 compromised LiteLLM event and is explicitly not an independently audited impact/remediation finding. This report has no common incident-discovery process or equal disclosure window across suppliers. It therefore cannot rank relative security from the presence of that one record or assume that an unrecorded incident never occurred elsewhere.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.supplier.mercor.incident](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.mercor.incident)

[analysis] Artifact attribution is nontransitive. Scale’s HelpSteer annotation, Translated’s multilingual role, Prolific’s recruitment case, Toloka’s U-MATH validation and Surge’s GSM8K collection are specific relationships. A paper citing a dataset, an author’s affiliation, a supplier’s general service menu or a benchmark family’s parent link does not establish another supplier contribution. The graph is sparse in explicit object relationships; many approved observations are typed text. A reader should not confuse catalogue richness with an exhaustive supplier-to-artifact map.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.supplier.scale_ai.helpsteer3-contribution](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.scale_ai.helpsteer3-contribution), [next.claim.helpsteer3.translated](evidence.html#assertion-next.claim.helpsteer3.translated), [candidate.supplier.prolific.cohere-recruitment](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.prolific.cohere-recruitment), [candidate.supplier.toloka.umath-validation](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.toloka.umath-validation), [candidate.supplier.surge_ai.gsm8k-contribution](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.surge_ai.gsm8k-contribution)

[method] Research governance: the publisher’s public identity discloses applications for paid work at some covered companies, membership in A.Team’s talent network and a separate proposed AI research lab. No profiled company has paid for coverage or is a customer, investor or affiliate of the publisher under that disclosure. External reviewer credit requires consent. This preparation claims actual separate AI source review and will require separate exact-report evidence-auditor and adversarial review; it does not claim human peer review or an external operational certification.

[research_gap] Governance unknowns include project-specific contracts, current assurance-report scopes, removal-request outcomes, consent withdrawals, subprocessor execution and worker appeal effectiveness. These cannot be resolved by treating a top-level license, policy statement or source-content review as an operational audit. Buyer diligence should obtain the relevant documents and test the actual project boundary; future research should record both support and unresolved limitations.

[analysis] Disclosure completeness is an observable governance input, while actual conduct remains a separate question. GIGO audits publication reporting in a selected literature; Who Annotates extracts task-level disclosures with an automated model and a separately adjudicated reference. Both reject equating missing reporting with absent practice. Their results justify asking for training, language proficiency, instructions and reconciliation records. They do not justify ranking a supplier’s ethics or data quality from how many public fields are filled.

Evidence IDs: [cohort9.claim.gigo.audit-limit](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.gigo.audit-limit), [cohort9.claim.gigo.instructions](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.gigo.instructions), [cohort9.claim.whoannotates.task-level-audit](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.whoannotates.task-level-audit), [cohort9.claim.whoannotates.adjudication](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.whoannotates.adjudication), [cohort9.claim.whoannotates.reporting-pattern](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.whoannotates.reporting-pattern), [cohort9.claim.whoannotates.audit-limit](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.whoannotates.audit-limit)

[analysis] A documented consent workflow does not finish privacy diligence. WildChat reports an agreement plus secondary confirmation and multilingual PII filtering, yet warns that hashed IPs and request headers can link conversations. The reported process was not independently tested here. For a proposed conversational-data use, examine the exact released fields, linkage routes, permissions and intended population; preserve the difference between a source’s stated control and demonstrated residual risk reduction.

Evidence IDs: [cohort9.claim.wildchat.consent-gate](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.wildchat.consent-gate), [cohort9.claim.wildchat.anonymization](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.wildchat.anonymization), [cohort9.claim.wildchat.selection-limit](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.wildchat.selection-limit)

[analysis] Public availability and private evaluation are separate diligence questions. Riemann-Bench is private; APEX-Accounting distinguishes private tasks and a small public development world; ALE has unresolved public-instance count wording; DAYJOB evaluates more finance tasks than its public finance release. None of these facts alone invalidates the scientific use, but each changes independent reproducibility and a buyer’s access obligation. Confidence is high in this distinction. Require a precise access manifest, permitted reproduction scope and complete task/attempt accounting; inspected payloads and executable grading checks would change reproducibility confidence.

[analysis] Rights evidence should follow each component. A paper’s benchmark declaration does not establish rights to every included chart, source image, copied repository or professional document. StarCoder explicitly retains license/opt-out detection limits; Chartography’s online provenance does not establish chart redistribution rights; the new VQA family reports a creator CC-BY release statement without a per-image audit. Confidence is high in the need to keep those scopes separate and unestablished for any particular buyer’s legal permission. [analysis] Versioned rights comparison — permission statements attach to different objects. GeneBench-Pro’s preprint carries CC-BY-NC 4.0 while its public case-study package declares MIT; CVDP separates non-code, original code and upstream components with two unspecified NOTICE entries; DeepResearch Bench II distinguishes evaluation code from task-specific licenses and later generated model reports. [analysis] A benchmark-use instruction can coexist with a permissive metadata license. GDP.xlsx preserves an Apache label beside directions excluding training and checkpoint selection. µ-MATH separates model-output license terms from other fields. AA-LCR licenses its questions while declining to claim rights over accompanying document text, and the Nexdata listings describe paid commercial access whose terms depend on the project. These observations support a component-and-use matrix covering questions, source media, traces, annotations, code and execution environments. They do not provide a legal reconciliation or blanket permission. Confidence is high in the disclosed scope distinctions; a rights judgment would require the actual applicable terms and permissions.

[analysis] Declared privacy and synthetic fixtures should be reported at the object actually described. EMRBench’s fixture is described as synthetic; RedlineBench describes fictional parties and scrubbed metadata; Nexdata’s hand-pose listing says facial-identifying information is absent. None of these observations is an independent consent, reidentification or downstream-use audit. The reasoning is to request a data-flow and provenance record for each delivered component rather than infer complete privacy protection from a category label. Confidence is high in preserving these public-source limits and unmeasured in any private payload’s actual properties. An authorized component-level inspection and project-specific provenance evidence could narrow those unknowns.

## 10. Buyer decision guides: use cases, pilot designs and acceptance

[method] The following are proposed buyer procedures derived from the reviewed evidence, not reports of completed supplier trials. They do not recommend a universal winner. Each use case states the required deliverable, a candidate responsibility model, a paid pilot and acceptance evidence. The buyer should pre-register critical errors, slices, exclusions, rework limits and decision rules before seeing outputs. Numeric targets should follow the buyer’s risk and uncertainty requirements; no universal accuracy threshold is invented here.

[analysis] Buyer use case 1 — Expert preference data for a specialized assistant: requirement and comparison. Specify prompts, candidate responses, domain credentials, language, independent judgments per item, preference strength and rationale fields. Compare a managed preference program with participant access only after assigning task design, recruitment, adjudication and acceptance. HelpSteer3, HelpSteer2 and InstructGPT show why final pair counts conceal different repetition and aggregation structures.

[analysis] Buyer use case 1 — Expert preference data for a specialized assistant: proposed paid pilot. Use a paid calibration batch spanning routine, ambiguous and deliberately difficult cases. Freeze the raw-label schema before consensus. Have a separate reviewer inspect disagreements and rejected items without knowing the supplier or initial majority. Keep duplicate prompts and ranked-set expansion identifiable, then hold out a second batch for acceptance.

Accept only against the predeclared target: valid independent judgments, traceable exclusions, correct domain-language intersections and adjudication supported by reasons. Report first-pass and final acceptance with all submitted items in the denominator. Do not let post-filter agreement substitute for coverage of difficult cases. Reject an unsupported claim that more released pairs necessarily means more independent human evidence.

[analysis] Buyer use case 5 — Medical, legal or financial expert data: requirement and comparison. Specify the permitted professional task, jurisdiction or clinical context, credential evidence, privacy boundary and intended model use. Do not transfer evidence from image annotation to clinical advice quality or from general finance work to jurisdiction-specific legal accuracy.

[method] Common pilot record: versioned brief; source and rights manifest; task/environment version; contributor qualification rule; raw judgments or trajectories; review and exclusion log; adjudication reasons; acceptance denominator; cost inclusions; and residual risks. Separate supplier process errors from buyer guideline defects, environment failures and model failures. The final purchase decision should state which evidence established suitability and which assumptions remain conditional. Keep unsuccessful pilots and rejected examples in the internal learning record so later comparisons do not inherit survivorship bias.

[analysis] Pilot refinement for expert preference and multilingual data: retain an unfiltered calibration sample alongside the accepted sample. Score raw agreement, exclusions, adjudication and acceptance separately; inspect whether difficult but relevant cases disappear. HelpSteer2’s κ change is conditional on multistage filtering, Aya’s language total does not guarantee uniform contributor diversity or safety review, and Inherent Disagreements warns against pooling batch-normalized scales. Predeclare whether the buyer needs consensus labels, calibrated scalar attributes or a distribution of valid preferences before requesting a price per example.

[method] A proposed statistical acceptance rule should make its assumptions explicit. For n independent randomly sampled units with zero observed critical defects, a one-sided 95% binomial upper bound is 1 − 0.05^(1/n); excluding a true defect rate p* at that confidence requires n ≥ log(0.05)/log(1 − p*). This is a design calculation, not an observed quality result. Repeated attempts, translations, shared source items and repeated participants can violate independence; use the original sampling unit and cluster-aware inference or report descriptive results instead. A zero-defect pilot does not prove zero population risk, and safety-critical controls can require a separate exhaustive gate.

[method] Proposed commercial acceptance record. Freeze the deliverable version, coverage matrix, rights/processing instruments, permitted subcontracting, rejection/rework rules, escalation path and payment basis before production. Require a complete manifest and reproducible checks for every accepted unit, plus a stratified blinded sample for substantive correctness. Log paid qualification and revision time separately from production units and include failed attempts, review and infrastructure costs in the project ledger. These are analyst-proposed conditions, not a representation that any named supplier has accepted them or that a pilot has occurred.

[analysis] Pilot refinement for original use cases 2, 5, 7 and 10 — separate evaluation integrity from score quality. Require a pristine grading boundary, reject attempts to read hidden references and test correct alternative implementations as well as deliberately invalid ones. DeepSWE’s separated verifier environment, ProgramBench’s cleanroom and dummy-binary filtering, and SWE Atlas’s no-op mutation checks suggest different falsification cases; none guarantees complete coverage. Confidence is high in retaining these controls and unmeasured for a particular supplier. Predeclare the critical false-accept conditions and inspect all exceptions. Independent adversarial execution on a frozen pilot would change acceptance confidence.

Flan and xP3 transform/reweight upstream material; Chatbot Arena Conversations pairs human winner votes with two model responses; ELOQUENT separately predicts preference classes and explanations. A stratified independent sample of the buyer’s actual use and a complete overlap audit would change confidence in reuse.

[analysis] Extension to the existing environment and software pilots. Freeze the exact task roster, container/dependency manifest, instructions, hidden references, judge version, tool access, time limit and repeat aggregation before comparing candidates. Terminal-Bench’s mutable dependencies, SWE-Marathon’s distinction between development feedback and hidden final checks, and APEX-SWE’s telemetry-based diagnosis without failing tests show why a single runnable-environment label is insufficient. The proposed acceptance exercise should separately record startup failure, infrastructure interruption, ungradable output, task failure and constraint violation, then challenge the scorer with a no-op and a valid alternate implementation. This is an extension of the retained pilot designs, not a newly executed trial. Confidence in any supplier remains unmeasured until the buyer’s own held-out acceptance results exist.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.normal12.terminal-bench.reproducibility-limits.v2](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.normal12.terminal-bench.reproducibility-limits.v2), [candidate.normal12.terminal-bench.verification.v4](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.normal12.terminal-bench.verification.v4), [candidate.next12.swe-marathon.task-format.v3](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.next12.swe-marathon.task-format.v3), [candidate.third11.apex-swe.observability-curation.v2](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.third11.apex-swe.observability-curation.v2), [candidate.third11.apex-swe.verification.v2](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.third11.apex-swe.verification.v2)

[analysis] Extension to the existing document and professional-work pilots. Preserve native deliverables and evaluate validity separately from substantive utility: PDFBench distinguishes a form’s strict pass from field-level correctness; RedlineBench requires a loadable Word redline and contextual attorney criteria; Harvey LAB separates deliverable existence from rubric satisfaction; PLE separates infrastructure reruns from runs with no gradable deliverable. A proposed pilot should include apparently polished artifacts with a critical missing field, prohibited edit, unsupported claim or invalid native structure, together with valid alternatives. These examples motivate acceptance design, not a forecast of legal, clinical or engineering job replacement. Confidence is high in the metric separation and unmeasured for a new deployment. Independent domain review of the buyer’s artifacts would determine whether the proposed checks are adequate.

[analysis] Extension to the existing supervised-data and feedback pilots. Request item-level prompt and response provenance, the exact selection/filter decision, any reference or test availability, raw and accepted denominators, and applicable component terms. AM’s verification-language conflict, s1K’s unresolved schema differences, SmallThoughts’ missing item-verification procedure and Multi-SWE-RL’s omitted manual phase make these concrete inspection targets. The proposed pilot should sample rejected and accepted items and independently inspect plausible false positives and valid discarded alternatives. No training or supplier comparison was executed for this report. Confidence is high in the disclosed documentation gaps; measured error, utility and cost require the buyer’s own matched experiment.

## 11. Research outlook: testable judgments and open questions

[analysis] Hypothesis — stage-level provenance will become a more useful comparison than a binary human/synthetic label. The sample already contains human-authored preferences, model-generated feedback, synthetic educational scores and human correction of model responses. Confidence is moderate for the usefulness of this distinction and unestablished for its effect on procurement outcomes. The hypothesis would strengthen if provenance-complete manifests predict fewer acceptance surprises on matched tasks; it would weaken if those details fail to add information beyond ordinary samples and contracts. This is a research proposition, not a forecast of market adoption.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.independent-human-labels](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.independent-human-labels), [next.claim.ultrafeedback.model_feedback](evidence.html#assertion-next.claim.ultrafeedback.model_feedback), [candidate.paperfull.fineweb.synthetic-educational-labels](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.fineweb.synthetic-educational-labels), [cohort5.claim.deepseekv3.human-check](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.deepseekv3.human-check)

[analysis] Hypothesis — environment and verifier maintenance will be a distinct recurring delivery burden. Refresh describes versioned verifiers, OSWorld announces a verified-version change, and SWE-bench Multimodal reports repeated-test filtering. Confidence is moderate that version and stability matter within these examples, but the corpus supplies no market-wide maintenance cost. A longitudinal study should record environment breakage, verifier corrections and acceptance changes under frozen agents. If stable tasks require little upkeep across relevant software changes, the hypothesized burden would be narrower than suggested.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.cohort4.refresh.versioned-verifiers](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort4.refresh.versioned-verifiers), [cohort4.dataset.claim.osworld.version-change](evidence.html#assertion-cohort4.dataset.claim.osworld.version-change), [cohort6.claim.swemultimodal.stability-appendix](evidence.html#assertion-cohort6.claim.swemultimodal.stability-appendix)

[analysis] Hypothesis — multilingual validity will require native task design as well as translation quality. M-IFEval modifies constraints, MENLO isolates local dimensions and BenchMAX post-edits translated data. Confidence is moderate for the methodological distinction, without an estimated commercial premium. A useful experiment would match translated, post-edited and native-authored tasks on intended constructs and independently score local failures. Equal validity under those controlled conditions would weaken the need for a separate native-authoring stage in that particular use case.

Evidence IDs: [cohort7.claim.mifeval.japanese-filter](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.mifeval.japanese-filter), [cohort7.claim.mifeval.objective](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.mifeval.objective), [cohort7.claim.menlo.dimensions](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.menlo.dimensions), [cohort7.claim.benchmax.pipeline](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.benchmax.pipeline)

[analysis] Hypothesis — reliability reporting will need both repeated execution and disagreement preservation. τ-bench distinguishes all-trials reliability from at-least-one success, while DICES and the disagreement study expose meaningful variation in human labels. Confidence is high that these are different denominators; the effect on supplier selection remains untested. A matched pilot should compare decisions made from aggregate success alone with decisions using repeated trials, raw labels and adjudication reasons. The hypothesis would weaken if added detail does not change acceptance or predict deployment errors.

Evidence IDs: [cohort4.claim.taubench.repeat-reliability](evidence.html#assertion-cohort4.claim.taubench.repeat-reliability), [cohort3.claim.dices.expert-crowd-difference](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.dices.expert-crowd-difference), [cohort3.claim.disagreement.instance-disagreement](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.disagreement.instance-disagreement)

[analysis] Hypothesis — reward-model and monitor evaluations will need adversarial separation from the optimization loop. Summarization overoptimization, verifier search exploitation and the reasoning-monitor study demonstrate specific mechanisms by which optimization can outpace a proxy. Confidence is moderate for the need to test this risk, not for its prevalence in current services. Hold out failure classes and reviewer inputs when optimizing the system, then measure independent outcome errors. A robust matched study showing stable external validity across optimization intensity would narrow this concern.

Evidence IDs: [cohort3.claim.summarize.overoptimization](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.summarize.overoptimization), [cohort2.claim.verifiers.search-limit](evidence.html#assertion-cohort2.claim.verifiers.search-limit), [cohort7.claim.monitor.optimization](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.monitor.optimization)

[analysis] Hypothesis — labor and documentation quality should be evaluated as operating processes, not only disclosure artifacts. CrowdWorkSheets asks for maintenance and pool-selection rationale; Datasheets asks about collection participants and compensation; the labor study warns about unknown population boundaries. Confidence is moderate for the research value of these fields, with no causal claim that publishing them improves wages or model quality. Follow-up research should compare documentation with consented worker evidence and project logs, retaining discrepancies and avoiding a disclosure-completeness score that masquerades as performance.

Evidence IDs: [cohort8.claim.crowdworksheets.maintenance](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.crowdworksheets.maintenance), [cohort8.claim.crowdworksheets.selection-rationale](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.crowdworksheets.selection-rationale), [candidate.paperfull.datasheets.worker-compensation-disclosure](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.datasheets.worker-compensation-disclosure), [cohort8.claim.latinlabour.representativeness](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.latinlabour.representativeness)

[research_gap] Priority evidence gaps: comparable accepted-unit economics; contributor-level paid-active windows; independent project outcomes; version-specific rights clearance; non-English and non-text coverage intersections; benchmark side-effect detection; and a complete source-supported supplier contribution map. The current graph’s richer catalogue does not resolve these automatically. Research should prioritize decision-changing evidence rather than optimize counts, and should document negative findings and unresolved cases alongside additions.

[method] The weekly outlook should be revised through falsifiable change conditions. Each stable executive finding records confidence, reasoning, limitations and what would change the assessment. New primary evidence can strengthen, narrow or supersede a finding; a changed source version should not silently overwrite its predecessor. A meaningful revision will identify which observed assumption changed and whether the effect is task-specific or supports a broader conclusion. No growth, revenue, employment or technology-adoption forecast is produced from this selected corpus.

[analysis] Hypothesis — a stronger documentation audit will improve diligence only if reporting signals are checked against project evidence. GIGO and Who Annotates observe disclosure, not undisclosed practice; the latter also exposes extraction uncertainty. Confidence is moderate in the need to distinguish those objects and unmeasured in the commercial value of an audit score. A follow-up could compare disclosed instructions, training and compensation fields with consented project records and independently sampled outputs. If completeness fails to predict agreement between disclosure and practice, its role should remain a transparency measure rather than a performance proxy.

[analysis] Hypothesis — complete-task reliability will be more decision-relevant than fractional rubric completion in workflows with decisive controls. APEX-Accounting, HANDBOOK.md and DAYJOB distinguish strict/relaxed or mean-criterion/repeated-complete metrics; PLE’s hybrid score exposes a different tradeoff. Confidence is moderate in the hypothesis and high that the metrics differ. A prospective workflow study should compare acceptance and downstream failure predicted by each metric under a fixed task population. If fractional scores predict accepted outcomes as well after severity and review costs are controlled, the proposed emphasis should narrow.

[analysis] Hypothesis — disclosure of excluded work and selected populations will improve procurement decisions more than larger raw row counts. Qualification self-selection, disagreement filtering, adversarial task screening and translated rows all change the effective denominator in the reviewed studies. Confidence is moderate in the decision relevance and unmeasured in commercial impact. A blinded buyer study could compare choices made from headline totals with choices made from full admission/exclusion manifests, then validate the selected service on independent work. No effect on selection accuracy or accepted cost would narrow this hypothesis.

[analysis] Testable judgment — release evolution can alter a score without a new logical family. AA-LCR repairs answer keys and warns against direct score comparison; DecoyCount distinguishes release withdrawals, stale derived answers and historical scores; Harvey LAB changes task rosters; DeepResearch Bench II changes the scored subset and judge protocol. The proposed hypothesis is that a meaningful portion of apparent score movement in an evolving evaluation could arise from these protocol or population changes. No fraction is estimated here. Confidence is high that matched-version replay is necessary and unknown about the contribution of each factor. Re-evaluating unchanged stored outputs under old/new scorers, then rerunning a fixed task intersection under fixed scaffolds, would separate these explanations.

[analysis] Testable judgment — downstream improvement needs a controlled training contrast rather than a promising environment specification. PostTrain Arena describes a fixed before/after held-out comparison, but its captured landing state pauses challenge runs and its later README distinguishes bounded pipeline checks from a completed held-out training run. The implication is methodological: freeze base model, compute, recipe, held-out suite and acceptance rules, then report repeated-run uncertainty before attributing a gain to contributed environments. This report asserts no completed PostTrain gain or supplier ranking. Confidence is high in the documented distinction and unknown for the intended program’s effectiveness. Actual accepted held-out runs with matched controls would supply the evidence that changes it.
